plan.thesis: A consequence model turns a loss of containment into physical effects. Associate owns HOW MUCH GETS OUT AND WHERE DOES IT GO (source terms and the Gaussian plume), Professional owns WHAT DOES THE FIRE RADIATE (the solid flame chain), Expert owns WHO IS HURT AND WHAT DOES THE ENGINE NOT KNOW (blast, probits, dropped scope, judgement). Each capstone grades only its own tier question.
plan.tierSplitDecision: The dispatch proposed Associate = source terms, Professional = dispersion, Expert = fire, explosion and probits. The engine structure argues otherwise and the split was adjusted: the fire section is the largest (burning rate, two flame lengths, tilt, three surface emissive powers, the view factor, transmissivity, the composite and a distance search) and is one chain from pool to heat flux, so it is one tier; dispersion takes its release rate from a source term, so the two are one question; blast and probits both end at harm to a person and the probits read every other section, so they close the course with the dropped scope. Expert with fire, blast and probits together would have carried three engine sections in six modules.

tiers.beginner: Associate: m01 what a consequence model computes (units, results and refusals, sources), m02 liquid through a hole, m03 gas through a hole (choked, subsonic, the critical ratio), m04 pools and evaporation (single route), m05 the Gaussian plume (Briggs sigmas, reflection, ppm and mg/m3), m06 how far the plume reaches (off axis, distance to a concentration, three states). Digest sections 1 to 13.
tiers.intermediate: Professional: m01 burning rate (Babrauskas, Burgess), m02 flame length (Thomas still air and with wind), m03 tilt and surface emissive power, m04 the view factor (the overhang refusal), m05 transmissivity and the heat flux (Bagster single route, the distance search, the point source seam), m06 the Yellow Book pool fire reproduced with its errata. Digest sections 14 to 22.
tiers.advanced: Expert: m01 TNT and Kinney and Graham, m02 the blast field and its inverse, m03 probits (thermal, overpressure), m04 toxic probits (two sources, two units, a changing concentration), m05 what the engine does not do (dropped scope, single route quantities, the approximate inverse probit), m06 judgement end to end and the seams. Digest sections 23 to 33.

openItems.engine defects: None found in the graded paths. The oracle replay agrees to 4.07e-13 relative on closed forms and roots, and every published value the digest reruns reproduces within its stated tolerance.
openItems.engine doubt: the inverse probit: probabilityToProbit and probitDoseForProbability bisect on the lib/stats Abramowitz and Stegun CDF (|error| <= 1.5e-7), so a dose read back from one percent is off the exact inverse by about one part in a million (0.139897 on the lees-chlorine one percent toxic load). Not a defect for a lethality band; it is why no inverse is graded. An exact inverse (Acklam or a Newton step on erfc) would remove it; owner decision, not needed for this course.
openItems.engine doubt: sourcing weaknesses taught: the Kinney and Graham Z range is borrowed from Kingery-Bulmash (FINDINGS 5); the Briggs advisory range is from memory of textbooks; the hydrogen golden gamma 1.405 is inferred; the CBU table is secondary. Each is taught as a judgement or an inference and none carries a graded answer beyond Kinney and Graham inside its range.
openItems.capstone design decisions: the dispatch proposed grading the one percent toxic dose; replaced by a Lees ammonia probability fed in mg/m3 at a stated temperature (the dose inherits the approximate inverse); the thermal probit value was replaced by the thermal lethality probability because every sibling integer count from 1 to 12 sits at a 0.5 tolerance and blocks a probit value in that range; the Purple Book ammonia preset was replaced by the Lees one because only Lees presets have an independent published check.
openItems.engine doubts from the key-truth audits: None touches a graded quantity. (1) poolFromSpill with no wall height skips the overtopping test and returns any depth as confined, silently (fails open). (2) plumeDistanceToConcentration carries no Briggs range warning on the distances it returns, and from a ground release its reported peak is the value at the 1 m search floor. (3) atmosphericTransmissivityBagster says 1e4 < pw x < 1e5 in its model string and accepts both endpoints. (4) poolFireSolidFlame takes the Bagster path as X - D/2 and ignores the tilt, so a flame leaning toward the target gets too long a path and too low a transmissivity on the (ungraded) Bagster route. (5) solidFlameDistanceForHeatFlux evaluates at maxDistanceM twice (no effect). (6) the engine inverse probit gives the OSD/30 TNO row one percent dose as 384.345053 against the golden exact 384.344943, the section 30 approximation at work.
openItems.panel coverage: FireExplorer exposes no Burgess, still air flame length or uc tile, and HarmExplorer's probit view takes psig; the audits rewrote the exercises to what the panels expose. Extending the panels is an owner choice.
